newsitem.title: USA: U.S. meat safety chief Michael Taylor resigns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. meat safety chief Michael Taylor resigns.

text.p: Michael Taylor, architect of revolutionary new meat safety rules, has resigned as the Agriculture Department's food safety chief just three months after the rules were completed, the department said Thursday.
The announcement had been expected for several weeks, with Taylor's staff saying he was happy to have taken the lead in designing the regulations but keen to let others implement them.
President Clinton regards the new rules as a major policy achievement, referring to them on the campaign trail and personally unveiling them at a White House ceremony July 6.

"He helped the Clinton Administration transform an outdated system into a state-of-the-art strategy for radically improving the safety of the food we feed our families," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said of Taylor.
The new rules mandate that meat and poultry slaughter and processing plants introduce scientific testing for sickness-causing bacteria over the next three years.
Taylor was a controversial figure who drew sharp criticism from a reluctant meat industry, which battled against his initiatives in Congress and in the courts.
